Widening doers.build to pass a Backend through follows the precedent researcher already sets. The enhancer would need a new plug point in loops/.

Each lab/solution folder runs on its own, start to finish, even if that means duplicate files across folders. solutions/sol1_enhancer (the Claude Code plugin) is the reference pattern: own Taskfile with no includes, no imports from the repo-root loops/ or solutions/ packages. Lab 1 was hand-redefined as a Claude Code plugin (commit 66573fc) and no longer matches what the generator would produce, so re-running it would clobber that work. Remove the lab1_enhancer entry from LABS_SPEC (or otherwise skip it), so labs 2 through 4 still regenerate normally but lab 1 and its solution family are left alone. scripts/build_done_branches.sh also references lab1_enhancer in its SLUGS array and will need the same exclusion once the done-m branches are retired.

Delete the four local branches, the four origin branches, and retire the build script.

All five also have a Taskfile.yml that is just an includes: block pulling in the root Taskfile. Copy the needed source (ticket.py, criteria.py, gates.py for the three tool variants; contract.py, roles.py, roleplan.py for the two runtime-port variants) into each folder as local files, point loop.py's imports at the local copies, drop _root.py where it is no longer needed, and replace each Taskfile.yml's includes: block with a small standalone one. solutions/sol1_enhancer (the Claude Code plugin) is already done and is the reference pattern; do not touch it.

Students following prompt 4 as written will rebuild the old bug.
set.title: Prompt 4 (Claude Code) is stale versus the solution's first-poll fix

set.acceptance_criteria: LGTM cannot move a ticket to state: ready unless check_fields.py (or the Judge agent) has already scored it as passing.
set.body: A human commenting LGTM currently sets state: ready and loop: implementer directly, with no rubric check. A two-line draft can be blessed by a human without the Judge ever scoring it. Ready should require the rubric to be green; LGTM should only be able to short-circuit further enhancer rounds after that, not replace the Judge.
set.title: LGTM marks a ticket ready without a Judge pass

set.acceptance_criteria: A script alongside check_fields.py enforces budget-exhausted and same-signature-twice as hard stops, independent of what the skill prose says.
set.body: SPEC.md admits the three exits (ready, budget spent, same-signature stall) are described in skill prose, not enforced by code. Module 1's own point is proving a hard stop in code, not trusting the model to honor a written rule. check_fields.py already computes missing fields in code; extend that pattern with a small script next to it that tracks budget and detects a same-signature repeat, so the stop is structural like the read-only scope already is.
set.title: Exit conditions are still skill text, not enforced in code
